## Task
Do A and B name the same business concept (the same real-world thing, so the classes model one concept under different names)? Concepts that merely share attributes such as an id or a date are not the same.

### A
concept: Club Booking
where: RinkService (uses), src/business/rinkService.ts, component business
code:
=====SOURCE-BEGIN
if (overlaps(c, session)) for (const h of c.halves) blocked.add(h);
=====SOURCE-END=====

### B

=====SOURCE-BEGIN
create(data: Omit<Booking, "id">): Booking {
=====SOURCE-END=====

response.rationale: These are different concepts. RinkService uses ClubBookingRepository.listByDate and, separately, BookingRepository.create/get/list/listBySession/update, so the two are stored and queried independently. A club booking has rink 'halves' that get blocked when it overlaps a session ("for (const h of c.halves) blocked.add(h);"), so it reserves part of the ice. A Booking is created with create(data: Omit<Booking, "id">) and is called from purchase, handlePaymentResult, expireOverdue and memberUses, which points to an individual paid place on a session. They share the word 'booking' but model different real-world things.
